content.comment_body: Hello everyone! I have some [product_name] devices ([article_no], FW: [version_no]), which I load with a program. After a power loss, the device time is not preserved. I wanted to ask if it’s possible that the internal capacitor is faulty from the factory. Thank you for any advice.
Forum members here may not be able to fully answer that. Please consider submitting a support request and contacting [company_name] directly.

Hello [user_name], Thank you for your response. I understand, and in the meantime, I already contacted the hotline regarding this. I am mainly interested to know if anyone else has experienced the same problem and managed to find a solution.

Personally, I haven’t encountered this issue. I am using a [product_name] with original firmware [version_no], later updated to [version_no]. From what I know, the device must remain connected to power for a certain time so the internal capacitor can fully charge.

analysis.insight_summary: A user describes a recurring issue where the device clock fails to retain time after power interruption, suggesting either hardware or backup battery problems. The user wonders if this could be due to a hardware defect and seeks confirmation from others who may have faced and resolved similar problems. Another community member mentions that the device requires sufficient time connected to power for its internal capacitor to properly charge, indicating a possible design requirement or expected limitation for reliable operation.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the device to maintain its clock settings reliably through brief or minor power outages without losing configuration. Clarification is sought on whether the observed behavior is due to a defect or an operational limitation, along with peer experiences or solutions.
pain_keywords: loss of time after power failure
